To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have established a cell-free system in which extracts from G(1) cells promote the sequential assembly of ORCs, Cdc6, and MCM proteins onto origin DNA in a stepwise fashion, and that extracts from mitotic cells are unable to support the binding of MCM proteins.
extracts from G1-arrested cells support sequential assembly of ORCs, Cdc6, and MCMs onto exogenously-added origin-containing DNA.
the assembly of prereplicative complexes (which contain the MCM2 to MCM7 proteins) on DNA in vitro is regulated by cell cycle-dependent changes in the activities of cyclin-dependent kinases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the initiation of DNA replication.
the initiation of DNA replication, a process that is essential for the propagation of all forms of life.
understanding how the initiation of DNA replication is regulated in eukaryotic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the initiation of DNA replication is an ordered process in which the assembly of the pre-RC is followed by its activation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the assembly of the initiation proteins onto the origin DNA occurs in a stepwise manner and requires ATP hydrolysis.

the initiation of DNA replication at yeast ARS elements is a two-step process in which pre-RC assembly is driven by the low Cdk activity that characterizes G(1) phase and origin activation is driven in a Cdk-dependent manner by the increase in cyclin activity at the end G(1) (see also refs. 2-4).
we describe a system to reconstitute in vitro the assembly of prereplicative complexes (or pre-RCs) on origin-containing DNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the budding yeast replication initiation system can be reconstituted from purified proteins and extracts prepared from cells arrested at various cell cycle stages.
we can reconstitute the assembly of preinitiation complex in vitro, and we can do it in a sequential manner.
it provides a system to study the mechanism and regulation that underlies the assembly of the prereplicative complex (pre-RC) in budding yeast.
